result.question: Give me a sample-by-sample picture of the fault gases in Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. For each sample, list hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Name the dominant gas, meaning the one with the highest ppm, and give its percentage of the five-gas total. Then tell me whether the dominant gas changed at any point in the window. Say what that shift points to, for example hydrogen pointing to partial discharge, ethylene to a hotter thermal fault, or acetylene to arcing. Also rank the five gases by their percentage growth from the first to the last sample. If a gas is null in a sample, leave it out of that sample's total and mark it as missing. If fewer than two samples have all five gases, give the ranking from the latest reading alone and say that no trend could be established.
result.answer:
All the data I need is in hand — four samples, none with null values — so no further calls are required.

**Transformer 1 (MAIN), 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 — fault-gas samples (ppm)**

| Timestamp | H₂ | CH₄ | C₂H₆ | C₂H₄ | C₂H₂ | 5-gas total | Dominant gas | Share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15T00:00 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32409 | Ethylene | 51.5% |
| 2024-01-16T00:00 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 32056 | Ethylene | 51.5% |
| 2024-01-17T00:00 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 32308 | Ethylene | 51.7% |
| 2024-01-18T00:00 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 32307 | Ethylene | 51.4% |

No gas was null in any sample, so nothing was marked missing.

**Dominant-gas shift:** None. Ethylene was the dominant gas in all four samples, holding a steady ~51–52% of the five-gas total. Because there was no shift, there is no change in fault signature to interpret — but the persistent ethylene dominance (with methane and ethane as the next largest) points consistently to a high-temperature thermal fault (>700 °C range) rather than partial discharge (which would be hydrogen-led) or arcing (which would be acetylene-led; acetylene is only 6–8 ppm here).

**Percentage growth, first sample (01-15) → last sample (01-18), ranked:**

1. Hydrogen: 2845 → 2900 ppm, **+1.93%**
2. Acetylene: 7 → 7 ppm, **0.00%**
3. Ethane: 5467 → 5450 ppm, **−0.31%**
4. Ethylene: 16684 → 16600 ppm, **−0.50%**
5. Methane: 7406 → 7350 ppm, **−0.76%**

All four samples had all five gases, so the trend is based on the full window. The movements are small (all within ±2%), so the gas profile is essentially stable over these four days — but the absolute levels of ethylene, methane and ethane are very high, which warrants attention independent of the flat trend.
